name: The False Haqim and the Assassins (Wolves at the Door)

pages.name: The False Haqim and the Order of Assassins

text.content:
Source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Two: Saracens

In 1192, the first Western victim of the radical Ismaili sect known as the Assassins fell to their daggers: Conrad of Montferrat, whose death sent shockwaves through the Crusaders and all of Europe. The sect traces its founding to Hasan-i Sabbah, an Ismaili leader who seized the mountain fortress of Alamut ("the Eagle's Teaching") in the Elburz Mountains shortly before the turn of the 12th century, and whose follower Bu Tahur Arrani assassinated the Seljuk vizier Nizam al-Mulk in 1092. Hasan-i Sabbah died in 1124, but his doctrine of absolute loyalty and obedience lives on among his followers.

The Assamites would like to deny all involvement with the Assassins, but cannot: the sect might never have arisen without the aid of a former @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} pawn, a ghoul who now mockingly calls himself Haqim, after the clan's own founder. The Assamites call him the False Haqim.

The False Haqim was once an @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} warrior's ghoul and protégé during the fifth through seventh centuries, chosen and trained for a singular gift: true sight, the ability to see past all illusions to the reality beneath them, making him his master's hunting hound against Obfuscated and disguised prey. When his master fell during a campaign against the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali}, the ghoul's blood oath recoiled and shattered his mind; he fled into the desert, and the Assamites who knew him assumed he had met an untimely end. In truth he survived, and over two centuries learned many of his master's skills — including how to recognize and destroy Cainites — while hunting down at least a dozen Assamites among his many victims. In time he recovered enough of himself to build a legend and a following from fragments of his master's tales, and when he heard of a place called Alamut, he claimed its mantle of leadership.

The False Haqim's direct control over Alamut and the Assassins is limited; he is a shadow ruler rather than an open commander, and most of the sect's actions are driven by the sectarian politics of Islam rather than his own design. Over the last century, however, he has recruited a small inner circle of men who share his gift of true sight; they hunt Cainites and return them to Alamut to sustain the ghoul-lord's unnatural longevity. The famous single killing stroke of the Assassins reflects his own lessons in driving a stake through a heart with one thrust. All @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} attempts to storm Alamut and remove this disgraceful rogue have failed, for even the deepest Obfuscate is like a tattered veil before the gaze of his students — and, ironically, because the False Haqim has quiet admirers within the Assamite clan itself, who have taken note of the Assassins' effectiveness at removing rivals within Islam and sowing terror among the Crusaders. Night by night, the methods and images of hunter and imitator grow more alike in the minds of Western Cainites.
